transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-21 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (CTO, BluePylon), Tom Keller (Head of ML Infra), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary:
BluePylon currently runs most inference on OpenAI with an internal vLLM fleet for cost-sensitive workloads. They are evaluating options to exit hosted provider dependency and standardize on a consistent runtime (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Main concerns: eval parity (TGI/vLLM), latency vs cost tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS/compliance, and networking/VPC for private deployments. BluePylon wants a short benchmark and a security package before a pilot.

Topics discussed:
- Migration strategy (hosted, dedicated, private)
- vLLM/TGI compatibility and parity testing
- Networking, VPC, KMS, and audit logs
- Cost/latency tradeoffs and batching/quantization options
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: alright everyone thanks for jumping on, this is Sophie from Redwood, joining with Daniel our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha: doing good, thanks. we'll try to keep it tight, we've got a bunch of internal folks who want to understand the risk if we move off OpenAI.
[00:12] Daniel: great, quick agenda—understand current infra, key success metrics, security constraints, then go into parity and deployment options. sound good?
[00:20] Tom: yes. quick context: BluePylon runs customer-facing summarization and search; most traffic hits OpenAI for quality, bulk offline runs use our vLLM cluster (we use TGI for some models). Our ask: can Redwood match quality, latency, and operational ergonomics, and what does the path look like to go from hybrid to either Redwood hosted or our private deployment.
[00:40] Sophie: perfect. first Qs—what are your targets for tail latency and cost per 1k tokens? any SLA expectations?
[00:48] Tom: tail latency < 300ms for short chat-ish prompts, and for higher-throughput batch jobs < 100ms isn't critical but throughput matters. Cost target is roughly 40% lower than our current OpenAI spend for batch workflows; for live traffic we're willing to pay more for latency.
[01:08] Daniel: good to know. on the parity front—do you have an eval prompt set we can run? will you need exact output parity or acceptable deltas?
[01:18] Aisha: we have a set of ~500 prompts and some scoring rules. exact token-for-token parity isn't required but we need no regressions on key business metrics (hallucination, safety filters). we'll provide the set.
[01:30] Sophie: great. operation questions—are you leaning on managed keys/KMS or do you need HSM? any data residency requirements?
[01:38] Priya: we need AES-256 at rest, KMS with customer-managed keys is preferred, and audit logs retained for 2 years. also SOC2 and ISO27k evidences are a must.
[01:50] Sophie: that's standard for Dedicated/Private — we can do CMKs and long retention; we'll share SOC2 artifacts after NDA.
[01:58] Tom: what's the network pattern for private? we have strict egress rules and an air-gapped-ish environment for some data, we've torn out direct internet access for PII workloads.
[02:08] Daniel: for Private deployment we can run a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC or an on-prem package; data paths never leave your network if you choose that route. there are nuances for model updates and telemetry—can be controlled or disabled.
[02:24] Aisha: how does Redwood handle model variants? we use TGI for some custom weights; can you host our custom tgi artifacts?
[02:32] Daniel: yes, we support bringing your model artifacts. runtime compatibility depends on format—if they're vLLM-compatible or Hugging Face torchscript variants, we can onboard. there might be differences in optimizer kernels which affect latency; we'll run a parity bench.
[02:48] Tom: and caching—we rely heavily on KV cache reuse for chat sessions. does Redwood preserve prefix caches across replicas?
[02:56] Sophie: yes, our serving runtime supports KV caches and we have strategies for sticky sessions or shared cache tiers to cut warm-start costs. Daniel can run through specifics after.
[03:08] Daniel: (laughs) yeah the TL;DR is we have continuous batching and prefix caching; if you have long convo contexts we can keep the KV alive to avoid regen. but it's configuration-heavy.
[03:20] Priya: can you talk about audit logging? we need user-level tokens and request logs that are tamper-evident.
[03:27] Sophie: we provide structured audit logs and integrate with common SIEMs; for Private you can ship logs to your own S3 with object-lock, or we can store and forward under an enterprise package.
[03:38] Aisha: what's the typical migration path? pilot on hosted then dedicated, or straight to private?
[03:44] Daniel: common pattern is quick pilot on hosted to validate model parity and latency, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private if you need network isolation or compliance. but some customers start Private for regulated workloads.
[03:56] Tom: question about quantization—we use 4-bit quantized vLLM variants. can Redwood run these without accuracy loss?
[04:04] Daniel: we support a number of quantization profiles and will recommend based on your eval; sometimes 4-bit has minor deltas on edge cases—our Optimize tooling will suggest tradeoffs.
[04:16] Sophie: for benchmarks, we'll run two tracks: 1) fidelity parity vs OpenAI and TGI/vLLM on your prompt set, 2) throughput/latency on the representative load. we'll share results in a spreadsheet.
[04:28] Aisha: good. and how do you handle fallback—if model variant isn't available due to capacity? we need graceful degradation.
[04:36] Daniel: smart routing policy—requests can fall back to a compatible model (cheaper or smaller) with rate-limiting and circuit-breaker rules; we can set hard SLOs for critical routes.
[04:48] Priya: legal and procurement—do you have a standard DPA with data residency clauses, and what's the turnaround?
[04:54] Sophie: yes, standard DPA and we work with your legal team; turnaround depends on redlines but typically 2–3 weeks for enterprise edits.
[05:02] Tom: there was a recent issue with our TGI fleet and OOMs during long sequence runs—how does Redwood prevent memory blowups with long KV caches?
[05:12] Daniel: memory management is a core part of our runtime—adaptive KV eviction, per-request memory quotas, and we profile sequence-length distributions to pick kernels. also, you can cap max response tokens for stability.
[05:24] Aisha: ok let's talk timing. we'd like to run a benchmark next week and decide on pilot by the end of the month. is that feasible?
[05:31] Sophie: yes. we'll aim to kick off the benchmark Tuesday, need your prompt set and a small sample dataset for throughput tests. Daniel will own the bench.
[05:40] Daniel: action item—I'll stand up a repo and run a paired run: OpenAI baseline, vLLM self-host baseline, Redwood hosted and Redwood dedicated sim. we'll collect latency percentiles and output diffs.
[05:52] Tom: perfect. small ask—can you show token-level cost breakdown? we need to compare unit economics to our vLLM op costs.
[05:59] Sophie: yes we'll include token-level cost and per-route model cost in the report; Optimize will suggest batching and cache settings to hit your 40% target for batch.
[06:10] Priya: last security question—the telemetry you collect, is it PI-free by default? we don't want prompts leaked to vendor logs.
[06:17] Daniel: by default we collect minimal telemetry for ops; for enterprise you can opt out of prompt retention and control metrics. for Private it's entirely in your control.
[06:26] Aisha: any known limitations around TGI plug-ins or custom kernels we should be aware of?
[06:31] Daniel: custom kernels can be integrated but require an onboarding step; sometimes we need to compile kernels per infra which adds time. we'll flag that in the SOW if you plan to bring proprietary runtimes.
[06:45] Sophie: ok wrapping up—recap and next steps: Sophie will send pricing and SOC2 artifacts (NDA first), Daniel will run the parity benchmark, Priya to share KMS/compliance doc, BluePylon to share prompt set. we'll schedule the SE deep-dive for networking. any other blockers?
[06:59] Tom: none from infra. timeline is tight but good.
[07:02] Aisha: sounds good. thanks!

(brief chat and confirmations for scheduling)

[07:30] Sophie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the repo links and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

End of call notes:
- Tone: pragmatic, engineering-led with security controls front-of-mind.
- Risk flags: need clear parity on hallucination metrics, potential kernel/quantization delta on 4-bit models, and egress/network constraints for private workloads.
- Deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2 artifacts, pricing deck, SE deep-dive on VPC/KMS.

References and links discussed (to be attached separately):
